newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO sees Euro costs at Dfl 500 mln.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO sees Euro costs at Dfl 500 mln.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Thursday that it expected to incur total costs associated with the introduction of the single currency in Europe of about 500 million guilders.
Management board chairman Jan Kalff said last August that Euro-related costs would be between 100 million and 150 million guilders over the ensuing four years.

An ABN AMRO spokesman said Kalff now expected the cost would amount to about 500 million "over the years", adding that this included provisions for automation projects such as the Global Transaction Services clearing and payments system.
"By far the largest part is for the Euro," he said.

But the spokesman stressed this should be taken as no indication of how much the bank would have provided for costs associated with the new currency in the second half of the 1996 fiscal year. It announces its results next Thursday.
ABN AMRO made a provision of 100 million guilders in the first half of 1996 for the introduction of the Euro, the introduction of a smart card and other automation projects.
Analysts expect more provisions for the second half of the year.
